Whether tucked away by tauren skepticism or by the Forsaken's own natural preference for the dark, this quiet refuge bridges Lordaeron's undead with their Kalimdor allies.

subzone:pyrewood-village.text: Pyrewood Village. Pyrewood Village is an isolated human settlement nestled in southern Silverpine Forest beneath Shadowfang Keep. Originally part of Gilneas before being stranded outside the Greymane Wall, its living residents harbor a horrific secret brought upon them by the mad archmage Arugal. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement. When King Genn Greymane chose to isolate his kingdom behind the massive Greymane Wall following the Second War, Pyrewood was left on the northern side. Cut off from their homeland, the townsfolk were left entirely defenseless during the Third War as the Scourge marched across Lordaeron. Though they managed to survive the initial wave of the undead, their true nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

subzone:ragefire-chasm-classic.text: Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Ragefire Chasm is a sprawling network of volcanic tunnels carved directly beneath Orgrimmar, accessible through the shadowy depths of the Cleft of Shadow. Despite being situated under the Horde's sovereign capital, these fiery caverns crawl with hostile troggs and a subversive coven of cultists loyal to the Shadow Council. Beneath the stone streets and fortified towers of Orgrimmar lies Ragefire Chasm, a treacherous network of magma-filled subterranean caverns. The tunnels recently became overrun by the savage Ragefire troggs, who pushed upward from deep subterranean fissures. Magatha Grimtotem of the tauren attempted peaceful diplomacy with the creatures, but her overtures were violently rejected. Left unchecked, the troggs threaten to tunnel further into the foundations of the city itself.

subzone:raptor-grounds.text: Raptor Grounds. Tucked into the dusty hills of the southern Barrens, the Raptor Grounds is a secluded valley claimed by the Sunscale raptors. Unlike ordinary wild beasts, the pack here exhibits an eerie, tool-using cunning and a compulsive urge to steal bright trinkets from nearby settlements. Located west of Northwatch Hold, the Raptor Grounds serves as the primary nesting territory for the Sunscale raptors. Travelers quickly discover that these creatures are far from mindless predators: they display an unnatural intelligence, fashioning crude shelters, assembling primitive tools, and coordinating their hunts. Driven by a relentless fascination with shiny and unusual items, the pack regularly raids passing caravans and Horde encampments, dragging coins, trinkets, and supplies back into their canyon dens.

subzone:ratchet.text: Ratchet. Ratchet is a bustling neutral port town run by the Steamwheedle Cartel on the eastern coast of the Barrens. Founded by chief engineer Gazlowe after he helped construct Orgrimmar, it serves as the primary maritime trade hub linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Perched on the arid coastline between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh, Ratchet offers safe harbor to anyone carrying coin. Founded by the entrepreneurial engineer Gazlowe following the Third War, the port arose from smugglers, exiles, and daring traders looking to exploit Kalimdor's frontier. It operates beneath the banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel, maintaining strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships like The Maiden's Fancy regularly ply the waters across the Great Sea to Booty Bay, transporting goods, mercenaries, and raw materials between continents. Local bruisers keep a watchful eye on the docks, ruthlessly thrashing anyone foolish enough to start a brawl and disrupt commerce. Despite its outward appearance as a boisterous merchant town of docks, taverns, and workshops, Ratchet harbors darker dealings. Overlooking the harbor from the hills above sits a secluded tower occupied by an open coven of warlocks, including figures like Strahad Farsan and Menara Voidrender. While townsfolk and sailors busy themselves with cargo manifests and goblin engineering, practitioners of the dark arts gather here unmolested to commune with demonic forces, untroubled by the moral restrictions enforced in traditional faction capitals.

subzone:ravaged-caravan.text: Ravaged Caravan. The Ravaged Caravan is a smoldering wreck located on the northeastern shore of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Once a supply convoy bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operations, it was ambushed and destroyed by local tauren determined to halt goblin exploitation of their homeland. Perched on a rise above Stonebull Lake, the Ravaged Caravan marks an early clash between the tauren of Bloodhoof Village and the encroaching Venture Company. Sent to deliver mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, the caravan was cut off and wrecked by tauren defenders before it could reach its destination. Despite the devastation, stubborn Venture Co. survivors still cling to the ruined wagons and smoldering crates, jealously guarding what little cargo remains.

subzone:razor-hill.text: Razor Hill. Razor Hill is the principal Horde settlement in central Durotar, nestled at the strategic crossroads between the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar. Centered around a prominent fortified barracks, it serves as the staging ground and training center for young orc and troll warriors testing their mettle in the harsh wilderness. Built at a vital geographical junction, Razor Hill connects northern Durotar with the coastal settlements to the south and the sprawling plains of the Barrens across the Southfury River. Dominated by its stone-and-timber barracks and classic orcish burrows, the settlement was established early in the founding of Durotar. Shortly after the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde into an ambush here under the guise of an emissary summit, an assault thwarted when Rexxar went in Thrall's stead. Today, the outpost stands fully fortified against further coastal incursions. Under the command of veteran officers like Gar'Thok, Razor Hill coordinates local defense against several looming threats. Human marine remnants still hold Tiragarde Keep along the eastern shoreline, while aggressive quilboar and harpy tribes harass local supply lines. Far more insidious is the presence of the Burning Blade cult, whose shadowy rituals and corrupted agents in the nearby crags are closely tracked and stamped out by investigators like Orgnil Soulscar.

subzone:razor-hill-watchtower.text: Razor Hill Watchtower. Perched on the red stone bluffs overlooking Razor Hill, this sturdy outpost serves as an early warning post for the heart of Durotar. Furl Scornbrow keeps a vigilant eye across the dusty plains and toward the coast, safeguarding the settlement below from encroaching threats. Constructed from thick timber and iron framing, the Razor Hill Watchtower guards the settlement of Razor Hill and the surrounding canyons. Durotar faces relentless threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders prowling the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists lurking in nearby crags. From this elevated vantage point atop the ridgeline, the lookout can spot approaching warbands, smoke signals, and incursions long before they reach the settlement gates.

subzone:razorfen-downs-classic.text: Razorfen Downs (Classic). Razorfen Downs is the ancestral burial ground and traditional capital city of the quilboar, nestled deep within giant thorny brambles in the southern Barrens. Recently, agents of the undead Scourge led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer seized control of the labyrinth, reanimating the quilboar dead and threatening to expand their dominion across central Kalimdor. Grown from the same towering, petrified vines as nearby Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs rests where the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan fell during the War of the Ancients. For generations, the labyrinth of thorns served as the sacred necropolis and seat of power for the quilboar, guarded closely by the mystics of the Death's Head tribe. To the quilboar, the dense briars are holy ground, soaked in the blood of their divine progenitor. The sanctity of the Downs was shattered when agents of the Scourge infiltrated the brambles. Amnennar the Coldbringer, a powerful lich serving the Lich King, subjugated the resident Death's Head quilboar and turned the ancestral resting grounds into an undead redoubt. Reanimated skeletons, shambling corpses, and shrieking banshees now prowl the Spiral of Thorns. Both the Horde in the nearby Barrens and emissaries from the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind view this growing pocket of Scourge power as a grave threat to the continent.

subzone:razorfen-kraul-classic.text: Razorfen Kraul (Classic). Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal thorns that sprang from the blood of the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan. Ruled by the ruthless crone Charlga Razorflank, this fortified labyrinth serves as a staging ground for bloody raids across the southern Barrens. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the colossal boar demigod Agamaggan perished battling the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. Wherever his sacred blood seeped into the soil of southern Kalimdor, massive, impenetrable thorn vines erupted from the earth. The quilboar, believing themselves the mortal progeny of the Great Boar, gathered within these dense briars to dwell and venerate his sacrifice. The dense mass known as Razorfen Kraul stands as their most revered redoubt, thick with quilboar warriors, beast trainers, and earth-shaping shamans.

subzone:razormane-grounds.text: Razormane Grounds. The Razormane Grounds form the forward encampment of the Razormane quilboar pushing eastward from the Barrens into central Durotar. Choked with sharp briars and the stripped carcasses of wild game, this bristling outpost serves as the frontline in the quilboars' unending clash with the orcs of Orgrimmar. Sprawling beneath the red cliffs of central Durotar, the Razormane Grounds mark the furthest eastern reach of quilboar expansion out of the Barrens. Entangled within thick brambles and surrounded by bleached bones, the encampment poses a constant danger to travelers along the Southfury River. The camp is led by figures such as Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle, who orchestrate raids against neighboring orc settlements and passing supply lines. Despite regular patrols dispatched from Razor Hill and nearby outposts, the Razormane replenish their ranks tirelessly, sprouting from the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

subzone:razorwind-canyon.text: Razorwind Canyon. Razorwind Canyon is a winding, rocky gulch split across the main road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. Infested by the aggressive Dustwind harpies, the canyon poses a persistent danger to travelers moving north toward the Horde's capital. Razorwind Canyon flanks the central artery linking Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, carving paths into both the eastern bluffs and the western scrublands toward Tor'kren Farm. The canyon is the nesting ground of the Dustwind harpies, territorial creatures that strike without hesitation at travelers who stray too close to their roosts. Their presence so near the capital's trade routes makes clearing out these gullies an ongoing necessity for the defenders of Durotar. Beyond serving as harpy nests, the twists of Razorwind Canyon function as hidden routes through Durotar's red rock hills. The eastern branch tunnels deeply into the crags, providing a passage through a cavern into Drygulch Ravine. Because the harpies roost on the high perches and descend in flocks, unwary adventurers traversing these passes can easily find themselves surrounded and cut down.

subzone:red-rocks.text: Red Rocks. Red Rocks is a towering sandstone bluff in northeastern Mulgore that serves as a sacred ancestral burial ground for the tauren. Here, the most valiant fallen champions are laid to rest, and young braves travel to its quiet heights to seek the wisdom of their forebears. Rising high above the plains of northeastern Mulgore, the crimson formations of Red Rocks mark a sacred threshold between the living world and the next. Tauren tradition reserves this solemn ground for their most valiant heroes—chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives founding and protecting Thunder Bluff. They are laid to rest here in honor, among the graves of their forebears. It is equally a place of spiritual beginning, where young tauren complete their rites of passage by honoring the ancestral graves and communing with the wind. The enduring peace of Red Rocks has been shattered by the Bristleback quilboar. Creeping out from their dens, these aggressive scavengers have infested the sandstone ledges and desecrated the ancestral graves with filth. This violation deeply affronts the spiritual traditions of Thunder Bluff. Shaman and lorekeepers now summon aid to cleanse the crags, driving out the Bristlebacks and reclaiming the sanctity of their resting dead.

subzone:rocktusk-farm.text: Rocktusk Farm. Rocktusk Farm is a small swine ranch situated in northern Durotar just down the road outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Tucked near the fortified approaches of the capital, the stead supplies vital meat and provisions to the city's inhabitants. Carved out of the arid soil of Durotar, Rocktusk Farm is dedicated to raising hardy swine suited to the rough desert climate. Due to Durotar's notoriously dry and stony ground, raising crops is difficult, making domestic swine farms an essential lifeline for feeding Orgrimmar's burgeoning population. Nestled close to the capital's fortified perimeter, the homestead enjoys a degree of safety rarely found in the harsh wilds of the red canyonlands.

subzone:rogues-quarter.text: Rogues' Quarter. The Rogues' Quarter is a dimly lit district in the southeastern wing of the Undercity. It serves as the staging ground for the Forsaken's scouts, assassins, and underworld operatives, along with the craftsmen who support them. Tucked away in the southeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Rogues' Quarter gathers the Forsaken's most cunning and lethal survivors. In life, many were thieves, cutpurses, or silent blades for the Kingdom of Lordaeron; in death, their expertise in stealth, poisons, and misdirection has been repurposed to protect the fledgling nation from the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. The district hums with quiet activity, offering a covert haven where operatives sharpen their daggers, brew deadly toxins, and hone clandestine skills. Beyond stealth and assassination, the Rogues' Quarter is home to the specialized trades that enable undercover survival. Artisans gather here to instruct travelers in leatherworking and skinning, turning raw hides into light, silent armor. The clatter of engineering benches echoes through the stone halls as tinkers assemble gadgets, while field medics and apothecaries provide instruction in first aid and vend lethal poisons essential for covert work.

subzone:rolling-plains.text: Rolling Plains. The Rolling Plains span the southern expanse of Mulgore, stretching between Bloodhoof Village and the border of the Barrens. These windswept grasslands are home to thriving herds of wildlife, but they are also a point of perpetual vigilance due to prowling centaur raiders and aggressive harpies. Spanning south from Bloodhoof Village toward the natural earthen gates leading into the Barrens, the Rolling Plains embody the vast open ranges of the tauren homeland. The area teems with wild game essential to the tribes, including prairie wolves, kodo herds, flatland cougars, and swift tallstriders. For young hunters proving their worth to the elders, these sweeping savannahs serve as an indispensable proving ground where tracking, patience, and reverence for nature are put to the test. Despite Mulgore's naturally fortified ring of bluffs, the Rolling Plains remain uniquely exposed to outside threats. It is the only frontier where aggressive centaur outriders have managed to push past defensive perimeters to harass passing travelers and hunting parties. Adding to the peril, a nest of predatory Windfury harpies roosts in the eastern crags, swooping down upon stray game and vulnerable nomadic camps.

subzone:royal-quarter.text: Royal Quarter. The Royal Quarter is the secluded seat of power within the Undercity, serving as the throne room for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Here, the Banshee Queen directs the Forsaken alongside her dreadlord enforcer, Varimathras, guarded by an elite cohort of Royal Dreadguards. Tucked away behind towering archways and shadowed corridors, the Royal Quarter—also known as the Hall of the Dark Lady—is the political and military nerve center of the Forsaken. Sylvanas Windrunner holds court in this cavernous subterranean chamber, plotting the survival of her free-willed undead and the destruction of the Scourge. Heavily armored Royal Dreadguards stand vigil along the dais, ensuring that uninvited guests and would-be assassins never reach their queen. Standing beside the Dark Lady is the nathrezim Varimathras, an unexpected and uneasy fixture in the heart of the Undercity. After siding with Sylvanas during the civil war in the ruins of Lordaeron to save his own life, the dreadlord pledged loyalty to her cause. From the Royal Quarter, he commands deathstalkers and coordinates defensive operations across the realm. While his tactical cunning serves the Forsaken well, his demonic nature leaves many Horde allies wary of his true allegiances.

subzone:scarlet-watch-post.text: Scarlet Watch Post. The Scarlet Watch Post is an isolated watchtower stationed in the rocky hills of northeastern Tirisfal Glades, just north of the Scarlet Monastery. Maintained by a vigilant garrison of Crusaders, its sole purpose is to safeguard the monastery's vulnerable northern flank against flanking assaults. Perched in the rugged heights behind the Scarlet Monastery, the Scarlet Watch Post serves as a critical early-warning bastion for the zealots below. While the southern road up to the monastery gate receives heavy traffic and fortifications, the rugged cliffs along Tirisfal's northern coastline provide a tempting back route for infiltrators. To eliminate this blind spot, the Scarlet Crusade maintains this fortified stone tower—one of several Crusader outposts scattered across Tirisfal Glades. Under the stern command of Captain Melrache, a mixed force of Neophytes, Vanguards, and devout Friars keeps ceaseless vigil over the cliffs, ensuring neither the Scourge nor the Forsaken can surprise the order from behind.

subzone:screaming-gully.text: Screaming Gully. Screaming Gully is the first sprawling subterranean cavern encountered just beyond the entrance of the Wailing Caverns. Bathed in unnatural fungal glow and shallow waters, it serves as the outer redoubt for the corrupted Druids of the Fang and their mutated beasts. Stepping through the threshold of the Wailing Caverns leads directly into Screaming Gully, an echoing chasm where the wind groans through subterranean fissures. Far from the arid Barrens above, the gully is choked with damp overgrowth, humid mist, and aggressive wildlife twisted by the Emerald Nightmare. The Fanglord Lady Anacondra oversees the chamber, surrounded by acolytes of the Druids of the Fang and vicious deviate raptors, while ancient snapping turtles like Kresh patrol the shallow waterways below.

subzone:scuttle-coast.text: Scuttle Coast. The Scuttle Coast is the wave-battered eastern shoreline of Durotar, situated between Razor Hill and Tiragarde Keep. The rocky beach is strewn with sunken wreckage from Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's Kul Tiras fleet, making it an active scavenging ground for the Horde and a lingering reminder of recent naval warfare. Running along Durotar's eastern edge out to the Great Sea, the Scuttle Coast earned its grim character during the invasion led by Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. When the Kul Tiras fleet assaulted the fledgling nation of Durotar, fierce battles with the Horde drove many human warships against the jagged shoals, smashing them into splintered hulks. Today, the shoreline is choked with barnacle-encrusted timber, broken rigging, and salvaged cargo barrels. For the nearby encampments of Razor Hill, the coast remains a lingering reminder of how close the Kul Tiran threat still lies. The name Scuttle Coast may refer to the sunken warships scuttled or grounded during the fighting, or to the swarms of crabs and makrura that pick through the rotting detritus. Shoreline wildlife and dangerous tides keep casual travelers away from the wreckage.

subzone:sepulcher.text: Sepulcher. The Sepulcher is the primary Forsaken settlement and stronghold in Silverpine Forest. Once an ordinary Lordaeron graveyard and burial crypt overlooking the western coast, it now serves as a fortified sanctuary for the Horde against surrounding regional threats. Perched in the hills above the Lordaeron coastline, the Sepulcher was originally a quiet cemetery and crypt alongside the western road. In the wake of the Third War, the newly emancipated Forsaken repurposed the ancient stone vault and its grounds into an essential outpost. Surrounded by hostile forces on all sides—the feral worgen to the south, wandering Scourge remnants to the east, and Kirin Tor wizards watching from Ambermill—the Sepulcher provides a rare haven of safety, supplies, and command for travelers marching through Silverpine.

subzone:sewers.text: Sewers. The Sewers are a sprawling subterranean drainage network that provides a secondary entrance directly into the Undercity. Cutting beneath the hills west of the ruined palace of Lordaeron, this conduit allows bat handlers and stealthy travelers to bypass the precarious elevators leading down from the throne room. Before the plague wiped out Lordaeron, these stone culverts served as the mundane sewer lines draining the royal capital. In the hands of Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, however, the runoff tunnels have been integrated into the Undercity's outer defenses. Emerging west of the surface ruins near a contested Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, the passage provides a level, direct slope inside. Forsaken bat handlers use this cavernous conduit to fly riders swiftly into the subterranean rings, avoiding the sluggish cage lifts entirely. Because it circumvents the heavily fortified surface courtyards, it remains a dangerous vulnerability that hostile infiltrators constantly seek to exploit.

subzone:shadow-grave.text: Shadow Grave. Shadow Grave is a stone crypt perched atop the sloping burial grounds above Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the physical awakening point where newly liberated Forsaken shake off the stupor of death and the Lich King's faded control. Tucked into the rocky foothills at the top of the graveyard slope above Deathknell, the Shadow Grave is a simple stone mausoleum with an extraordinary purpose. Inside its damp vaults, corpses raised into the mindless servitude of the Scourge gradually awaken to free will. Under the watchful eye of caretakers like Undertaker Mordo, these freshly liberated undead stand up from their stone slabs and take their first shuddering steps into a world that despises them, setting out down the footpath toward Deathknell to pledge themselves to the Banshee Queen.

subzone:shining-strand.text: Shining Strand. The Shining Strand is the strip of shoreline hugging Lordamere Lake along eastern Silverpine Forest, stretching south from the Ruins of Lordaeron toward the rugged foothills of Alterac. Its shallows are home to settlements of aggressive Vile Fin murlocs, making the lakeshore dangerous ground for unseasoned travelers. Running along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest, the Shining Strand borders the misty waters of Lordamere Lake. The Vile Fin tribe of murlocs has established several aggressive settlements along these shallows, posing a deadly hazard to anyone attempting to travel the lake road, while feral worgen roam the deep woods of Silverpine behind the shore.

subzone:shrine-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Perched atop the highest peak northwest of the Valley of Trials, the Shrine of the Dormant Flame is a secluded sanctuary revered by Horde shaman. Guided by its solitary keeper, Telf Joolam, initiates make the treacherous climb to commune with the element of fire and prove their spiritual mastery. Reaching the Shrine of the Dormant Flame requires braving a narrow, winding trail that begins along the Southfury River at the southwestern edge of the Southfury Watershed. High above the red cliffs of Durotar, the mountain summit offers a commanding view of the surrounding lands, though a single misstep along the precipice means certain death. In this quiet refuge wanders Telf Joolam, a solitary hermit tasked with overseeing sacred rites. For aspiring orc and troll shaman undertaking the ritual Call of Fire, the shrine's brazier serves as the crucible where they must ignite slumbering coals using the ember of a vanquished elemental, proving their power to commune with and respect the destructive spirits of flame.

subzone:shrine-of-the-fallen-warrior.text: Shrine of the Fallen Warrior. Perched upon a secluded ridge west of the Crossroads lies the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, a quiet memorial overlooking the sweeping red savannahs of the Barrens. Marked by a stone plinth bearing the initials 'MK' and the body of a fallen orc warrior, it is watched over by the gentle presence of a Spirit Healer named Koiter. Tucked away high upon the hills northwest of the Crossroads, the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior stands as an unusually solemn haven amidst the dust and peril of the Barrens. To find it, travelers must scale a winding ridge pathway southwest of the summit until they reach a gentle mound. Upon the summit rests a carved stone monument, its plinth carved with the initials 'MK'. Before it lies the armored form of an orc warrior at rest, watched over day and night by a named Spirit Healer known as Koiter. There are no battle horns here, only quiet contemplation honoring a champion who walked Kalimdor's lands. Within the world, the shrine stands as an enduring tribute to a departed champion of the Horde whose soul lingers in the care of the spirits. Outside the realm, the monument serves as a heartfelt tribute created by the game's artists to honor Michel Koiter, a beloved illustrator who passed away during the development of the world. The resting warrior is modeled precisely after Koiter's own beta character, Twincruiser, immortalizing his presence forever beneath Kalimdor's open skies.

subzone:skittering-dark.text: Skittering Dark. The Skittering Dark is an abandoned mine and shadowy woodland hollow in western Silverpine Forest. Infested by aggressive giant spiders, the cavern and its surrounding woods are thick with webbing and danger for unwary beasts and travelers. Tucked into the hills just east of the western coast of North Tide's Run, the Skittering Dark was once a working mine. Today, the shafts are completely choked with cobwebs, serving as the sprawling nest of giant spiders. With the shadowy weaver Krethis haunting the exterior, the spiders hunt anything that strays too close.

subzone:skull-rock.text: Skull Rock. Skull Rock is a cavern tucked into the eastern coastal cliffs of Durotar, just east of Orgrimmar. It serves as a fortified coven for the demonic Burning Blade cult right under the capital's nose. Hidden beneath the crags of northeastern Durotar, Skull Rock is one of the most perilous strongholds of the Burning Blade cult in the region. Dark cultists, fel-worshipping orcs, and summoners gather deep within the winding tunnels to practice demonic arts and weave conspiracies against the nascent Horde. The cell is led by the dangerous warlock Gazz'uz, whose operations pose an imminent threat to the nearby gates of Orgrimmar and travelers traversing the eastern shoreline.

subzone:sludge-fen.text: Sludge Fen. Sludge Fen is a toxic industrial oil field operated by the Venture Company in the northeastern Barrens. Once a pristine, crystal-blue pool, the wetland was transformed into an oily quagmire after the goblins erected drilling platforms and machinery. The operation is overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle and attracts constant industrial espionage and sabotage from rivals in Ratchet. Before the arrival of the Venture Company, Sludge Fen was an untainted pool of crystal-clear water fed by natural springs in the arid Barrens. Driven by the relentless pursuit of profit, the Venture Company constructed an extensive oil-drilling operation over the basin, despoiling the wetland into a sludge-filled reservoir coated in heavy industrial waste. Overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle, goblin drillers, engineers, and overseers pump crude oil around the clock, heedless of the environmental ruin. The waters are now thick with runoff and toxic byproducts, leaving the native aquatic life choked beneath the grease.

subzone:solliden-farmstead.text: Solliden Farmstead. Solliden Farmstead is an active human pumpkin farm nestled in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of Deathknell. It represents a rare anomaly in northern Lordaeron: living native farmers who survived the Plague of Undeath and cling fiercely to their soil under the shadow of the Scarlet Crusade. While most of Lordaeron fell to ruin and rot, the fields of Solliden Farmstead still produce healthy crops. Today, these surviving human farmers live under the watchful shield of the Scarlet Crusade patrolling from a nearby tower. Traumatized and insular, they defend their homestead with unyielding hostility, striking at any outsiders who draw near—Horde and Alliance alike. To the Forsaken just emerging from Deathknell, Solliden is both a threat and a resource. The Royal Apothecary Society eyes the farm's pristine pumpkins as prime organic testing material for brewing their New Plague. Meanwhile, Forsaken officers like Deathguard Simmer send fledgling recruits to raid the fields, steal those pumpkins for Apothecary Johaan in Brill, and teach the living a lesson.

subzone:south-tide-s-run.text: South Tide's Run. South Tide's Run is the lonely southwestern coastline of Silverpine Forest, stretching along the cold waters of the Great Sea. Flanking the forested interior, these damp sands and surf serve as the southern complement to North Tide's Run. Stretching along the southwestern edge of Silverpine Forest, South Tide's Run forms a desolate boundary between the woods and the Great Sea. Unlike the protected eastern roads that lead down toward the Greymane Wall, this open shore takes the brunt of the western tides, serving as a bleak coastal wilderness largely untouched by the settlements inland.

subzone:southern-gold-road.text: Southern Gold Road. The Southern Gold Road is the vital desert thoroughfare stretching through the southern half of the Barrens, linking the central plains to the Great Lift. It serves as an indispensable artery for regional trade, carrying caravans, supplies, and wayfarers traveling between distant reaches of Kalimdor. Officially beginning at the stone bridge dividing the northern and southern halves of the Barrens, the Southern Gold Road runs directly south until it meets the Great Lift leading down into the Thousand Needles. Like the northern portion simply named the Gold Road, this dusty highway derives its moniker from the endless stream of lucrative merchant caravans that trek along its length. Despite constant harassment from local quilboar tribes and predators prowling the savannah, it remains one of the busiest long-distance paths on the continent, ferrying goods between remote outposts and bustling ports. The road sees travel far beyond local Horde traffic. Adventurers and hardy traders journeying to and from places as far-flung as Gadgetzan in the southern deserts of Tanaris, Auberdine along the misty shores of Darkshore, and the sacred groves of Nighthaven in Moonglade tread this sun-baked expanse. For travelers journeying on foot through Kalimdor's interior, surviving the journey down the Southern Gold Road is a grueling rite of passage.

subzone:spirit-rise.text: Spirit Rise. Spirit Rise is the northwest mesa of Thunder Bluff, serving as the tauren capital's premier sanctum for spiritual and shamanic study. Overseen by spiritual guides such as the Skychaser tribe, it features sacred training halls above and descends into the cavernous Pools of Vision below. Perched high upon the bluffs overlooking the plains of Mulgore, Spirit Rise is devoted to communion with the elements and ancestor spirits. Connected to the central mesa by rope bridges, it houses the Hall of Spirits and the Spiritual Healing pavilion, where young and veteran shaman gather to deepen their connection with the earth, air, fire, and water. The Skychaser tribe maintains a strong presence across the rise, guiding seekers through ancient traditions. Beneath the breezy huts and open-air totem shrines lies an entrance burrowing into the mesa itself: the steamy Pools of Vision, a sacred subterranean cavern where seers peer into spirit-touched waters.

subzone:spirit-rock.text: Spirit Rock. Spirit Rock is a sacred crag perched in the rugged bluffs above the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Reached by a winding trail known as the Hidden Path, it serves as a secluded holy site where initiates commune directly with the elemental forces of the land. Overlooking the red canyon where young Horde warriors and scouts begin their training, Spirit Rock stands as an altar of communion. Isolated from the clatter of the Valley of Trials, it is approached only via the Hidden Path winding up the rocky ridgeline. Aspiring shaman make pilgrimages to this desolate outcrop to drink the traditional sapta, piercing the veil of the physical world to hear the rumblings and whisperings of the earth itself.

subzone:stagnant-oasis.text: Stagnant Oasis. The Stagnant Oasis is one of the precious bodies of water nestled in the arid heart of the Barrens, positioned between the Gold Road and the Merchant Coast. Ringed by lush palms and contested by Kolkar centaur, its murky waters and surrounding shores sustain unique local wildlife, including snapping turtles and wandering kodos. Tucked away east of the Gold Road and inland from the Merchant Coast, the Stagnant Oasis provides a vital pocket of greenery amid the dusty scrubland of the Barrens. Like its neighboring waters, the pool supports dense foliage and aggressive snapjaw turtles, while weakened Barrens kodos often stray here away from the massive herds of the Field of Giants. However, travelers must tread carefully: Kolkar centaur maintain encampments along its banks, fiercely guarding the water rights against any who wander into their territory. Despite its stagnant appearance, the pool teems with unusual aquatic life, including strange mutate variants like Deviate Fish. Scholars and shamans keep a watchful eye on the Barrens oases, studying the peculiar forces affecting the local springheads and the wildlife that drinks from them.

subzone:stillwater-pond.text: Stillwater Pond. Stillwater Pond is a quiet, stagnant body of water resting just west of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Once a beloved picnic and swimming spot for the living children of Lordaeron, it has decayed into a murky pool inhabited by skeletal fish and prowled by dangerous scavengers. Before the Third War and the ravages of the Plague of Undeath, Stillwater Pond served as a tranquil retreat for the folk of Tirisfal Glades. Families from nearby hamlets gathered on its grassy banks for afternoon picnics, and children too young to brave the treacherous depths of Brightwater Lake learned to swim in its shallows. Today, the idyllic waters have turned lifeless and gray. The living have long vanished, leaving only skeletal fish darting beneath the surface and wandering undead drifting through the surrounding woods. Though quiet compared to the besieged roads and contested farms of Tirisfal, Stillwater Pond holds its own perils. The murky waters provide water only to the blighted beasts of the glades, most notably a ferocious darkhound named Bayne who stalks the shoreline. Travelers cutting through the western meadows on their way toward Brill must tread carefully, as predatory beasts and aimless zombies frequently linger along the water's edge.

subzone:stonebull-lake.text: Stonebull Lake. Stonebull Lake is a serene, horseshoe-shaped body of water wrapping around Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. Fed by the pristine natural runoff of the plains, it provides vital fresh water, abundant fish, and peaceful shores for the young tauren coming of age under Cairne Bloodhoof's guidance. Curving around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, Stonebull Lake defines the geography of central Mulgore. A wooden bridge crosses the lake's narrowest stretch, carrying the main dirt road between the settlement and the great mesa of Thunder Bluff to the north. Its calm waters are filled with native fish, making its banks a favored spot for resting hunters, weary travelers, and apprentice fishers learning their trade under the sweeping open sky.

subzone:the-den.text: The Den. The Den is the sheltered cave at the heart of the Valley of Trials in southwestern Durotar. Serving as the primary base of operations for young orc and troll adventurers, it provides martial and magical training before they set out into the wider world. Tucked into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials, the Den serves as an austere proving ground. Within its carved, shadowy interior, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters report to veterans like Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. It is here that fledglings receive their foundational combat instruction, supplies, and initial rites of passage, hardening them for the harsh realities of Durotar and the greater struggles facing the new Horde. Beyond housing class trainers and provisions, the Den functions as an active field redoubt. Between dispatching new recruits to cull the local beasts and aggressive quilboars, the overseers maintain a strict, vigilant watch over the valley.

subzone:thorn-hill.text: Thorn Hill. Thorn Hill is a fortified Razormane quilboar enclave nestled on the high ridges east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The settlement serves as a forward base for quilboar warbands raiding Horde supply lines traveling between Durotar and the interior savanna. Perched on the north face of the rugged hills between Durotar and the Crossroads, Thorn Hill commands a watchful vantage over the primary trade corridors of the Barrens. The settlement is home to a dangerous gathering of the Razormane tribe, including hunters, trained wolves, and earth-shaping geomancers. Guided by mystics like Elder Mystic Razorsnout, the quilboar here have escalated their attacks against passing Horde supply caravans. Because this mountain camp sits so close to vital transit routes, the guards at the Crossroads consider Thorn Hill one of the most immediate military hazards in the central savanna.

subzone:thunder-ridge.text: Thunder Ridge. Thunder Ridge is a rugged canyon in western Durotar, situated just southwest of Orgrimmar along the banks of the Southfury River. Once a lush grove of ancient trees inhabited by herds of thunder lizards, the canyon has suffered severe deforestation from human lumber operations and dark sorcery. Today, the agitated beasts and lingering cultists pose an ongoing threat to nearby settlements. Not long ago, Thunder Ridge was a rare green haven in arid Durotar, sustained by ancient trees. Its tranquil balance shattered shortly after the Third War when human interlopers from Kul Tiras began felling its timber, driving the native thunder lizards into a frenzy. Later, fel sorcery wielded by the Burning Blade finished the destruction, stripping the canopy and leaving behind a barren, exposed gorge where angry lightning-spewing beasts now roam unrestrained.

subzone:thunderhorn-water-well.text: Thunderhorn Water Well. Thunderhorn Water Well is a vital water source situated in the rolling plains of central Mulgore along the path between Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff. Like all the wells across the valley, it provides essential nourishment to the tribes and the herds roaming the grasslands. Keeping this water clean and defended is crucial to maintaining life in the tauren homeland. Situated amid the sprawling grasslands of central Mulgore, the Thunderhorn Water Well taps directly into the pure aquifers feeding the valley. For the nomadic tauren and their newly settled villages, these communal wells represent life, sustenance, and the Earth Mother's bounty. Because water is precious across the sun-drenched plains, controlling the wells means controlling the land itself. Intruders such as the Venture Company have repeatedly eyed these sources, attempting to harness them for industrial exploitation and disrupt the fragile balance the tribes fight to preserve.

subzone:tidus-stair.text: Tidus Stair. Tidus Stair is a natural rock formation of broad, stepped stone terraces perched over the Merchant Coast southeast of Ratchet. Sheltered beside the Great Sea, it serves as a quiet retreat for two tauren shamans communing with the tides and water spirits. Descending toward the surf southeast of Ratchet, the Tidus Stair resembles a monumental set of weathered stone steps cut directly into the coastal bluffs. While the surrounding Barrens are arid, dusty, and prone to skirmishes, this quiet stretch overlooking the Merchant Coast is dominated by the sound of crashing waves. Perched on the terraces is a modest hut where the tauren Islen Waterseer and Mahren Skyseer reside. Far from the bustling trade docks of the goblins, the two spend their days fishing, watching the horizon, and seeking insight from the coastal water spirits.

subzone:tiragarde-keep.text: Tiragarde Keep. Tiragarde Keep is a fortified human stronghold situated along Durotar's Scuttle Coast, south of Razor Hill. Originally built during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion, the ruined citadel remains garrisoned by hostile Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict. It serves as a defiant, permanent thorn in the Horde's side right on their home territory. Erected during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's campaign to eradicate Thrall's newly founded realm, Tiragarde Keep provided the Kul Tiran fleet an entrenched beachhead on the red shores of Durotar. Although the Horde eventually broke the siege and killed Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, the keep was never fully abandoned. Resupply forces under Lieutenant Benedict reclaimed the shattered stone walls, following the late Admiral's standing orders to wage an unyielding war against the orcs, entirely refusing the peace forged by Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Today, the keep's gleaming white battlements stand in harsh contrast against Durotar's crimson cliffs. Well-trained Kul Tiras sailors and marines patrol the ramparts and launch raids targeting supply lines near Razor Hill. For the Horde, Tiragarde Keep is an ongoing security crisis and a live proving ground. Orc and troll commanders constantly task young warriors with assaulting the fortress and cutting down Benedict's soldiers, seeking to contain the garrison before the humans can mount a deeper inland offensive.

subzone:tor-kren-farm.text: Tor'kren Farm. Tor'kren Farm is a quiet, struggling swine farm in northwestern Durotar, near Thunder Ridge and the Southfury River. Misha Tor'kren tends the homestead while anxiously awaiting news of her son Kron, who has not returned from a hunting trip. Carving out a living from the dry, unforgiving red dirt of Durotar is never simple, but Tor'kren Farm has had a harder time than most. Situated southeast of Thunder Ridge, the homestead focuses on raising pigs in a rugged climate where feed and water are scarce. Unlike the bustling trade posts or heavily defended barracks of the Horde, the farm stands isolated and quiet, producing meager yields in the shadow of nearby bluffs. Misha Tor'kren's son Kron went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River several days ago and has not returned. She had warned him about the vicious predators, but he left in anger. Now she asks passing adventurers to search for him or bring back a sign of his fate, fearing the worst but unable to begin mourning without knowing what happened.

subzone:trade-quarter.text: Trade Quarter. The Trade Quarter forms the central core of the Undercity, resting directly beneath the lifts from the Ruins of Lordaeron. It functions as the beating economic heart of the Forsaken, housing their primary bank vaults, auction market, and essential civic services. From this concentric hub, vaulted corridors branch outward into the surrounding districts. Descending from the shattered surface of Lordaeron, travelers step off the lifts into the echoing stone expanse of the Trade Quarter. Designed around a tiered, circular layout, its central platform holds the city coffers and central bank, framed by bridges spanning noxious runoff canals. Surrounding terraces buzz with vendors, guild registries, and auctioneers bargaining amidst the eerie gloom. Even basic accommodations reflect Forsaken pragmatism: the local inn offers unlined wooden caskets rather than soft beds. From this central nexus, stone archways lead outward into the city's specialized quarters, making it the unavoidable crossroads for any business conducted within the capital.

subzone:valgan-s-field.text: Valgan's Field. Valgan's Field is an abandoned wheat farm nestled in northern Silverpine Forest, overlooking Lordamere Lake. Once a picturesque homestead, it now lies desolate and overrun by the feral Moonrage worgen unleashed by Archmage Arugal. Situated just west of the Shining Strand and north of the nearby river, Valgan's Field was once a prosperous wheat farm offering scenic views of Lordamere Lake. That peaceful life vanished when the Scourge tore through Lordaeron, forcing its owner, Valgan, to flee or meet his end. Left untended, the ruined structures fell into the claws of feral Moonrage worgen prowling down from Shadowfang Keep. Before the Third War, the mage Arugal spent time here, leaving behind remnants of his arcane research that now draw the attention of the Forsaken.

subzone:valley-of-honor.text: Valley of Honor. The Valley of Honor serves as the martial core and warrior district of Orgrimmar, nestled in the northeastern canyons of the capital. It houses the city's barracks, warrior and hunter guilds, and the battlemasters directing Horde forces across Azeroth. With active forges, training rings, and quiet waters, it is where the Horde hones its strength and remembers its martial heritage. Situated behind high canyon ridges, the Valley of Honor acts as Orgrimmar's primary military quarter. Here, the clatter of practice weaponry and the ringing of blacksmith anvils define daily life. The Hall of the Brave dominates the valley, serving as a gathering point for seasoned warriors and battlemasters coordinating campaigns across battlefronts like Alterac Valley and Warsong Gulch. Flanked by training facilities for beastmasters and hunters, the district is dedicated entirely to equipping, drilling, and mobilizing the Horde's frontline defenders. Beyond arms and drill grounds, the valley supports the logistics of war. The Burning Anvil and Red Canyon Mining supply armor and raw iron, while engineers tinker nearby in Nogg's Machine Shop. Between duties, grunts and visiting adventurers cast a line into the valley's surprisingly serene secluded pool, offering brief moments of calm away from the dusty bustle of the Valley of Strength.

subzone:valley-of-spirits.text: Valley of Spirits. Tucked against the western cliffs of Orgrimmar, the Valley of Spirits serves as the long-standing seat of the Darkspear tribe within the Horde's capital. Filled with thatched lodges, tiki poles, and serene pools, it offers a stark contrast to the surrounding red stone and iron-clad orcish architecture. Branching westward off the bustling Valley of Strength, the Valley of Spirits is a lush and quiet enclave dedicated to the Darkspear trolls. When the tribe settled in Durotar alongside Thrall's orcs, this tranquil pocket among the crags became their urban gathering place. Trollish craftspeople, spiritualists, and practitioners gather around its wooden bridges and winding waters, practicing their arts away from the dry heat of the main thoroughfares. Beyond its dwellings and tranquil pools, the valley hosts practitioners of magic and wild crafts. Witch doctors, herbalists, and spellcasters congregate in lodges like the Spirit Lodge and Darkbriar Lodge. Tucked toward the back is the Talon Gate, which opens directly toward the open plains of the Barrens, offering quick passage for wanderers, hunters, and travelers roaming beyond the canyon walls.

subzone:valley-of-strength.text: Valley of Strength. The Valley of Strength is the bustling central commons of Orgrimmar, greeting all who pass through the city's towering front gates. Housing the city bank, the central auction house, and the Broken Tusk inn, it serves as the beating commercial and administrative heart of the Horde capital. Step past the fortified timber gates of Orgrimmar and you enter the Valley of Strength. Carved deep into the red canyon rock of Durotar, this valley serves as the Horde's front square. Adventurers, merchants, and warriors from all allied nations mingle across its dusty plazas, swapping war stories over flagons from the Broken Tusk inn or attending to vital trade at the central bank and auction house. It is a bustling testament to the strength and unity the orcs fought to establish in their new homeland. Beyond its defensive significance, the valley functions as the capital's foremost marketplace. Shops such as Soran's Leather and Steel Armory sell armor, while various vendors supply provisions for long treks across the Barrens. Grunts stand vigilant watch at every corner, directing newcomers and ensuring order among the diverse peoples who have taken refuge beneath Thrall's banner.

subzone:venomweb-vale.text: Venomweb Vale. Venomweb Vale is a shadowed valley in eastern Tirisfal Glades, sitting just south of the Scarlet Monastery. Once a lush woodland teeming with game, the vale has devolved into a blighted nest overrun by aggressive, venomous arachnids. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, this valley was a peaceful retreat of lush grass and verdant trees, favored by local hunters tracking deer and rabbits. Today, rot and creeping gloom dominate the landscape. Giant, venomous spiders swarm among the trees and hollows, led by the monstrous arachnid Sri'skulk. The vale's northern edge borders the territory of the Scarlet Crusade, where darkhounds prowl near the fortified Scarlet Encampment under Lieutenant Sanders.

subzone:venture-co-mine.text: Venture Co. Mine. Tucked into the eastern cliffs of Mulgore, the Venture Co. Mine is an unauthorized industrial excavation run by greedy goblin opportunists. Despite being denied rights by the tauren, the Venture Company dug into the hills regardless, threatening the natural balance of the plains. When the Venture Company sought rights to strip Mulgore of its minerals, the tauren flatly refused. The corporate cartel ignored them, tunneling deep into the eastern mountain wall anyway under the direction of Supervisor Fizsprocket. Their sprawling complex features three entrances—a ground tunnel guarded by hired muscle, a sheer cliffside overlook, and an upper passage leading out to a small lumber camp. The encroaching machines, smoke, and slag heaps represent a blatant defilement of sacred land.

subzone:war-quarter.text: War Quarter. The War Quarter is the northwestern district of the Undercity, serving as the command post and martial training ground for the Forsaken. Within its echoing stone chambers, the soldiers, priests, and crafters of Lordaeron hone their weapons and shadow magic in defense of their fledgling kingdom. It houses training halls for warriors and priests alongside weapon masters and heavy industry. Occupying the northwest sector of the subterranean metropolis, the War Quarter stands as the bastion of martial strength for the Forsaken. Beneath its gloomy stone arches, rank-and-file guards and elite champions assemble to drill in armed combat. Unlike traditional barracks of living kingdoms, this military center combines ruthless iron warfare with the chilling rites of shadow, housing an ominous Altar of Darkness where spiritual discipline merges with military ambition. Beyond housing warrior and priest guilds, the quarter functions as the heart of Undercity's wartime production. The clatter of blades and armor echoes continually against the stone, supported by the district's blacksmiths, smelters, and weapon masters. Here, iron forged deep in the earth is shaped to outfit the forces defending the ruins of Lordaeron from the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade.

subzone:whispering-forest.text: Whispering Forest. The Whispering Forest is a secluded, mountainous woodland nestled behind the steep cliffs west of Deathknell. Largely cut off from the rest of Tirisfal Glades, it harbors uncanny wildlife, a mysterious fairy circle, and deep-seated corruption sleeping far beneath the soil. Tucked away behind Northface Rock and Bandarion Keep, the Whispering Forest feels entirely alienated from the surrounding plague-touched kingdom. While it contains afflicted deer and roaming predators, it also features a tranquil lake and a strange ring of giant mushrooms, glowing with an uncanny energy beneath a hovering cloud of mist. The ghostly Knight of Mourning wanders the fairy circle, bound there by oath, amid a natural magic that seems to defy the Scourge-ruined land.

subzone:whispering-shore.text: Whispering Shore. The Whispering Shore is a somber stretch of coastline in western Tirisfal Glades, resting just north of the Solliden Farmstead. Once a tranquil and bountiful retreat for Lordaeron's fishermen, its cold waters have since been overrun by a violent tribe of murlocs. Before the Third War swept across northern Lordaeron, the Whispering Shore was renowned among locals as a favored fishing haven, celebrated for its calm waters and plentiful catches. Today, the chilling spray of the Great Sea crashes against an empty coast stripped of its peaceful past. The waters have grown cold and dark, devoid of their former bounty, and any unfortunate traveler wandering down from the hills risks being ambushed by territorial coastal dwellers. The beach is now firmly claimed by a band of hostile murlocs who ruthlessly attack anyone approaching the surf. Led by a fierce chieftain named Muad, these aquatic scavengers guard the shallows and tidal flats aggressively, posing a constant danger to nearby roads and the nearby Solliden Farmstead.

subzone:wildmane-water-well.text: Wildmane Water Well. The Wildmane Water Well is the northernmost of the sacred water wells scattered across Mulgore, resting just north of the mesas of Thunder Bluff. Vital to the plains and their herds, it has become a contested flashpoint targeted by goblin opportunists seeking to choke the tauren's lifeblood. For generations, the nomadic tauren have relied on sacred water wells dug across the golden plains of Mulgore to sustain their people and their wandering kodo herds. The Wildmane Well guards the northern expanse just beyond the shadow of Thunder Bluff. Its vital importance makes it an irresistible target for enemies of the tribes. The goblins of the Venture Company have fouled it with their poisons in a bid to control the regional water supply, and only a cleansing ritual with a totem crafted by the tauren can make its waters pure again.

subzone:windfury-ridge.text: Windfury Ridge. Windfury Ridge is a rugged highland area flanking the pastures of Mulgore. Notorious for harboring vicious harpies alongside predatory wolves and cougars, it poses a constant hazard to travelers while offering prized feathers to tauren artisans. Windfury Ridge rises sharply above Mulgore's serene plains, serving as the hunting grounds of the Windfury harpies. These vicious winged creatures nest high along the crags, readily swooping down upon any unwary wanderers who skirt the hills. The rocky terrain is further populated by prowling prairie wolves and wild mountain cougars, making the ridge one of the more treacherous borders of the tauren heartland. Despite the danger, the harpies are frequently hunted by brave tauren warriors; their vibrant, iridescent plumage is highly sought after across Thunder Bluff to adorn ceremonial garments for lavish feasts and wedding celebrations.

subzone:winterhoof-water-well.text: Winterhoof Water Well. The Winterhoof Water Well is a vital fresh water source situated on the edge of the Rolling Plains in southern Mulgore. Crucial to the local wildlife and nomadic tauren tribes, the well has recently fallen under threat from the exploitative Venture Company, who seek to poison and control the region's water supply. In the arid stretches of central Kalimdor, water is life, and Mulgore's subterranean wells sustain both the herds of the plains and the encampments of the tauren. The Winterhoof Water Well, named for one of the respected tribes of the plains, taps into the deep aquifers beneath the Rolling Plains. Unfortunately, its strategic importance has drawn the avarice of the Venture Company. Rather than sharing the land or negotiating, the ruthless goblin cartel has attempted to poison the water supply to exert leverage over the surrounding territory.
